title: Donald A. Codling et al. v. Presbytery of Eastern Canada
disposition_detail: The complaint was sustained on grounds 1, 4, 5, and 6, but not sustained on grounds 2 and 3. The General Assembly adopted a recommendation strongly urging Presbytery to reexamine Harris for licensure.
first_summary: Presbytery members challenged Eastern Canada Presbytery’s denial of Ron Harris’s licensure. The complaint was sustained in part because Presbytery improperly changed its voting rule during the meeting and its objections concerning counseling, evangelistic preaching, and sovereign grace did not justify denial. Claims that pertinent data was excluded and that requests to hear Harris preach were blocked were not sustained. The Assembly urged Presbytery to reexamine Harris.
summary: Presbytery members challenged Eastern Canada Presbytery’s denial of Ron Harris’s licensure. The complaint was sustained regarding the improperly adopted supermajority rule and the insufficiency of objections concerning counseling, evangelistic preaching, and sovereign grace; claims that pertinent data was excluded and requests to hear Harris preach were blocked were not sustained. Citing the fragmented examination and sharply differing views, the Assembly urged a complete reexamination at one meeting. It did not order Harris licensed or formally remand the matter.
